steps.title: Accepting, repairing or rejecting generated Python on evidence

segments.label: Repair a generated discount helper using expected results
segments.summary: A generated discount helper runs successfully and returns 80 for a price of 100 with a 20% discount. That result hides a mistake: the helper subtracts 20 as a fixed amount rather than calculating 20% of the price. With a price of 200, it returns 180 instead of the required 160. The repair calculates the discount amount as price multiplied by discount divided by 100, then subtracts that amount. Assertions for both expected results pass after the repair. Generated code and one passing test are not enough to establish correctness; acceptance needs evidence that the behavior matches the requirements.

blocks.group_title: Decide from requirements and test evidence

bridge.before: Watch how one passing test hides a requirement mismatch, while a second input exposes it. Focus on the evidence supporting correction and verification, not the generated origin.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates a requirement mismatch and verified repair, but not failed assertions, unexpected exceptions or unsafe-operation rejection. The text explains how those findings affect correction and rejection decisions.
